guarantees.claim: threshold_hit_q is cleared to 0 on asynchronous reset (negedge rst_ni).
When threshold_hit_clr is high (and not in reset), threshold_hit_q is cleared to 0, regardless of the state of threshold_hit.
When threshold_hit is high and threshold_hit_clr is low (and not in reset), threshold_hit_q is set to 1.
guarantees.cond: rst_ni high, threshold_hit_clr low, threshold_hit high

guarantees.claim: When none of reset, threshold_hit_clr, or threshold_hit conditions are true, threshold_hit_q retains its previous value.
guarantees.cond: rst_ni high, threshold_hit_clr low, threshold_hit low

assumptions.claim: The logic driving threshold_hit and threshold_hit_clr must ensure that a threshold_hit event is not lost due to simultaneous assertion of threshold_hit_clr, if every hit must be captured.
assumptions.cond: When threshold_hit and threshold_hit_clr are both asserted at the same time
assumptions.risk: A fault condition signaled by threshold_hit could be missed, potentially masking an entropy health failure and compromising security.

uncertain_points.claim: If threshold_hit is a short pulse or threshold_hit_clr is asserted too early (possibly in the same cycle as threshold_hit or before software samples), the hit could be cleared without being recorded, leading to an undetected entropy health violation.
uncertain_points.cond: threshold_hit event overlaps with threshold_hit_clr assertion, or software clears before reading threshold_hit_q
uncertain_points.risk: Undetected entropy health failure could allow weak keys or biased entropy to enter KMAC processing.
